Status: Wave 321 accepted (6.3): the CoAP client/server collaborators

Method.evidence: Class1069 (CoapClient) and Class1070 (CoapServer) were named in wave 319 from their own logger literals; this wave takes their collaborator contracts and accessors from 6.4. Interface44 is ICoapReceiver (6.4 CoapServer's icoapReceiver_0 auto-property holds it and its accessor pair takes and returns it), Interface37 is IOscoreSecurityContextProvider (6.4's securityContextProvider field) and Class1147 is CoapConfiguration (6.4's configuration field and a constructor parameter of both classes). The eleven accessors follow 6.4's readable field names (transmissionManager, messageCreator, securityContextProvider, configuration, coapReplayProtectionModule_0) and its auto-property pattern, and one is an exact method match: Task<Class1034> a(ushort) is ReserveUnicastEndpointsAsync(ushort preferredPort) -> Task<IoTTransportLayerConnection>.
Method.themes: The CoAP stack's own types were already named, so this wave names its collaborator surface. Class1070's remaining free rows are the obfuscated 6.4 members (method_8/11/12/13, the display-class callbacks) and compiler-generated list/CTS accessors with no vendor name; Class1079 (CoapTransmissionManager) has the same shape and needs its own pass.
